messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That likely refers to the standard error of the mean under the null hypothesis. The standard error (SE) = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention "null hypothesis test" maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under the null hypothesis. That is indeed SE = sigma / sqrt(n). They gave sample_std_dev = 1.4, sample_size = 40. So SE = 1.4 / sqrt(40). sqrt(40) ≈ 6.3249. So SE ≈ 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2215. So the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test is about 0.2215.

But maybe they want to calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test statistic? Actually the test statistic t = (sample_mean - population_mean) / (sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size)). The denominator is the standard error. So the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test statistic is 1 (for t distribution with df=39). But they ask "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" which is ambiguous. But likely they want the standard error of the mean. So answer: ~0.2215.

We can also compute the p-value using the function. But they didn't ask for p-value. They asked for standard deviation. So we can compute SE. Let's do that.
